nodes.label: A component

nodes.label: The import's rules
nodes.shape: the meter path rewrite (v1.3.1 → v1.4.0), the top-up link, eight text rules, the article number line; each stops the import when its anchor moves

nodes.label: R1
nodes.text: Declining a page as “not relevant” leaves it in the persona's reading list. open() auto-keeps an article on first open; decline() refunds the charge but does not undo the auto-keep, so the article stays under “Its reading list” and profile() adds +5 for it while the decline subtracts 2: a page the reader rejected pulls its topics up.

nodes.label: R2
nodes.text: restore() checks that the file has a numeric balance and a log array and nothing else. A persona without on[] and off[] makes the personas and newsroom views throw and show nothing; a log entry's path is rendered as the history link's href as it is; a persona's theme is written into a style attribute as it is. The file is the reader's own, so the exposure is a file someone else sent them to restore.

nodes.label: R3
nodes.text: A malformed percent sequence in ?session_id= (for example %E0%A4%A) makes decodeURIComponent throw inside onReady, so the element fails with “did not load: URI malformed” instead of saying the reference is missing.

nodes.label: R4
nodes.text: A reading share or a subscription sent from this site is labelled sgit.ai: the imported config has share.site = "sgit.ai" (so the text begins “My reading on sgit.ai”), subscribe.js writes From: site@sgit.ai, and the contact file says site: sgit.ai. The agent that drains the lane can tell the two sites apart only by the Sent from line.

nodes.label: R5
nodes.text: On the live site the lane for shares and subscriptions is on dev.send.sgraph.ai and the study page's vault frames come from dev.vault.sgraph.ai. Both hosts are named “dev”. Production reader data goes to them.

nodes.label: R6
nodes.text: Money is kept to a tenth of a penny and shown to a penny. Balance and spent are each formatted on their own, so a half-penny state shows, from £5.00, a balance of £4.95 and £0.06 spent, which do not add up; the history shows 5.5p. A reader who checks the arithmetic finds a penny missing.

nodes.label: R7
nodes.text: picks() excludes every page in the log, whichever persona read it, while profile() is per persona. An article read as Morgan is never picked for Rowan.

nodes.label: R8
nodes.text: feed() caches a failed fetch as null for the life of the page, so one transient failure leaves “The list of articles could not be loaded” on every view until a reload.

nodes.label: R9
nodes.text: If sgit.ai renames an article (a new slug), ids.py marks the old number withdrawn and gives the article a new number. A reading list that named the old number then says the article is no longer published, although it is.

nodes.label: R10
nodes.text: Every imported page loads assets/site.js, subscribe.js and shots.js by fetching the text and running it with (0, eval)(text) (the loader's bridge path), and the loader and the meter config are inline. A script-src policy without 'unsafe-eval' and without hashes breaks every page. frame-ancestors cannot be set in a meta tag at all, and GitHub Pages sets no headers, so framing (the Keep, Remove and Top up buttons under another site) is not prevented today.

nodes.label: R11
nodes.text: The one workflow ran validate.js only; the browser tests (46 + 65 checks) never ran in CI.

nodes.label: R12
nodes.text: The account pages, subscribe, the contact file and the component base are imported from sgit.ai on every sync and cannot be changed here except by a recorded rule, and verbatim files (scripts, JSON) cannot be changed by rule at all. R4 is the first consequence. The newsroom's meter is v1.4.0 while sgit.ai's is v1.3.1.

nodes.label: R13
nodes.text: The export includes the payment references (sessions, topups[].ref) that the share deliberately leaves out. A reader who sends their export instead of their share sends them.

nodes.label: R14
nodes.text: sessions[] and topups[] grow without bound, and a payment reference is not checked for shape before it is stored.

nodes.label: R15
nodes.text: persona(id) falls back to personas[0], which is “me” only when “me” is first; after a restore that puts another persona first, an unknown id resolves to that persona.

nodes.label: R16
nodes.text: Imported pages load the meter as sg-meter.js?v=<sgit.ai's release>, so the cache-buster never changes for a release of this site. That is fine while a published version is never edited in place, which is the rule; it is written here because v1.4.0 was edited in place while it was being built.

nodes.label: R17
nodes.text: A list's persona is keyed by a 32-bit hash of the names and numbers, so two different lists can share one persona with probability about one in four billion per pair.

nodes.label: R18
nodes.text: The landing view adds a window hashchange listener per element and never removes it, and re-renders on every meter change (the picker's “Copied” label resets).
